palm-600.note: The brand's own green and the system's second mark, taken from the pure vegetarian badge and the deck's regional headings. Scope is narrow and stated: the pure vegetarian mark, the Karnataka regional key, and an opening status. Never a section ground, never prose. palm-700 is the text floor on bone, palm-400 on ink.

display.purpose: The wordmark in the hero leaf. Once per page at most.

headline.purpose: Section headings, capped at 22-26ch so they break as two or three balanced lines.

title.purpose: Panel headings, form headings, card names.

lead.purpose: The one-sentence statement under a display or headline, set in Eczar regular so it reads as prose set large.

body-small.purpose: Register row glosses, captions, secondary notes.

label.purpose: Nav, buttons, column headings, ruled captions. Uppercase Archivo at 0.19em.

label-small.purpose: Margin glosses and micro-captions at 0.625rem. The floor of the label register: nothing in this system sets uppercase 0.19em type below it.

data.purpose: Days, dates, telephone numbers; anything that must align in a column. Tabular figures.

indic.purpose: A city's or the brand's own script, per-language Noto Serif with a real lang attribute.

subhead.purpose: Fixed upper step of the title tier at 1.5rem. Franchise support headings, locator outlet names, the wordmark from sm up.

entry.purpose: Fixed lower step of the title tier at 1.35rem, and the workhorse of every ruled register.

indic-entry.purpose: An Entry set in an Indic script at 1.65rem, one step above its Latin counterpart by the Indic Optical Step Rule.

seal-display.purpose: The struck city on the brass plate at 2.35rem. One-off step for the single focal element.

figure.purpose: A menu price. Archivo tabular figures at 0.9375rem with 0.06em tracking. The data register's 0.625rem step loses to a 1.35rem dish name, and a price is primary information rather than register furniture, so the register is allowed this one larger step. 0.9375rem is already on the ramp as Body Small, so this widens where the data register may be set rather than adding a size.

shadows.name: lift-leaf
shadows.purpose: A sheet of paper laid over the building. Hero-scale surfaces over photography.

shadows.name: lift-panel
shadows.purpose: A panel resting on paper. Detail panes, forms, cards.

shadows.name: brass-plate
shadows.purpose: The seal: raised top edge, dark seated bottom edge, plate shadow beneath a 168deg four-stop brass gradient.

shadows.name: struck
shadows.purpose: Type engraved into the brass plate rather than printed on it. Only used on a plate.

motion.name: ease-almanac
motion.purpose: The single shared ease. Every transition and keyframe in the system uses it.

motion.name: rule-draw
motion.purpose: Register rows and hairlines drawing in, staggered 70ms per row.

motion.name: seal-press
motion.value: 1200ms; scale 1.5 rot -14deg blur 8px -> scale 0.97 rot 1.5deg -> settled
motion.purpose: The brass plate landing on the page.

motion.name: rail
motion.purpose: The brass assurance marquee. Pauses on hover and focus-within.

motion.name: morph
motion.purpose: The script morph between an Indic and a Latin reading.

motion.name: link-brass
motion.purpose: The brass underline growing under a text link on hover or focus-visible.

motion.name: reveal-protocol
motion.purpose: Content is visible in authored markup; JS arms then plays. A failsafe sweep shows anything left armed.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce flattens all reveals, stops rail/lamp/kolam, cuts morph transitions to 1ms, locks settling morphs to their Latin reading

materialStops.note: Not palette colours. Gradient stops and texture alphas only; never applied to text or as a fill.

iconSystem.note: No icon font, no emoji, no text-glyph arrows. Marks are shrink-0 by default.

carriedOutsideSystem.reason: Nothing. The ten unimported shadcn primitives in src/components/ui/, src/lib/utils.ts, and the lucide-react, @base-ui/react, class-variance-authority, clsx and tailwind-merge dependencies have all been deleted. components.json is kept so a primitive can be re-added and restyled into this world on demand.

regionalKey.purpose: Colours a dish's provenance by its state so four states read at a glance without a legend and without a fifth hue.
regionalKey.scope: The small provenance line beneath a dish name only.

ornamentSet.admissionTest: Every ornament is a real object in the building. The diya hangs in the dining room, the thoranam is strung across the awning, the gopuram is printed on the cups and carry bags.

removed.name: BananaLeaf
removed.reason: The thali photographs already carry the leaf, so a drawn one would have been applied decoration rather than structure.

ornamentSet.emblemNote: LotusRoundel is a lotus cradled in two open hands. The side petals are written at their rotated coordinates rather than wrapped in a transform or a <use>, so a page holding several emblems depends on no shared id.

revealProtocol.attributes: Authored content carries data-reveal. The provider adds data-armed="true" (hiding it) only once JS runs, then data-shown="true" to play.
rules: Only data-shown may end the cycle. The scan selects [data-reveal]:not([data-shown]) and must NOT exclude armed nodes: the effect runs twice in development and again on route change, and a scan that skipped armed nodes leaves every below-the-fold element stranded at opacity 0 behind a disconnected observer.
A MutationObserver re-runs the scan so subtrees mounted later by client components still get armed, observed and shown.

The failsafe sweep runs on scroll, resize, load and a 1200ms settle. Scroll matters: a card parked off screen horizontally in a snap rail is vertically in view but never intersects, so without it the card stays invisible until the rail is dragged.
revealProtocol.auditTest: Scroll a page to the bottom, then evaluate document.querySelectorAll('[data-reveal][data-armed="true"]').length. It must be 0 on every page at every width.

narrative.overview:
The whole system is a South Indian daily almanac: a bone paper page with hairline ruling, one entry per day, the day that matters struck in red, and the important announcement pressed into brass. The building supplies the materials rather than a mood board: chocolate signage ink, granite plinths, brass lettering, the diamond jaali screen, the lotus roundel, the temple corbel and the lotus-bud eave course. Everything decorative in this world is structural somewhere in the storefront first.

Density is editorial, not promotional. Long prose measures (46-62ch), generous section rhythm (6/8/10rem vertical), and ruled registers instead of card grids. The page argues in sentences and hairlines; it never sells in tiles. Colour is nearly absent by volume: bone ground, ink type, granite for anything muted, and two marks - brass for the metal and kumkum red for the day. There is one locked light theme with no dark variant and no toggle; dark passages exist as ink-800 grounds inside the light world, never as an alternate skin.

The signature gesture is bilingual: a word arrives in its own Indic script and resolves into Latin a beat later, and hovering brings the script back. Motion elsewhere is arrival only - content is legible before any script runs, and reveals add the arrival rather than gate the content. Confirmed rejections: the category-default dark full-bleed food hero with a centred sans headline over a grid of dish cards; kickers and eyebrows above headings; decorative section numbering; gradient text; glass as decoration; icon fonts and emoji.
keyCharacteristics: Bone almanac paper with a laid tooth under every flat fill, so no ground reads as screen
Effectively square corners (0.125rem) and hairline ruling instead of boxes
One metal (brass), one festival mark (kumkum red), no second accent
Three type registers only: Eczar display, Alegreya prose, Archivo label and data
Every ornament authored as SVG from the building; no glyph, no emoji, no icon font
Warm ink-tinted shadows with offset and soft blur; never neutral black
One locked light theme by design

rules.name: The Single Metal Rule
rules.body: Brass is the only metal in this world. No silver, no copper, no second accent hue. If something needs to feel valuable, it becomes brass or it becomes ruled - it does not become a new colour.

rules.name: The Brass-700 Floor Rule
rules.body: Brass on text below 0.875rem must be brass-700. brass-500 and brass-600 are for marks, hairlines, carets and icons. This is why the brass ramp has five steps instead of three.

rules.name: The 4.5:1 Worst-Ground Rule
rules.body: Every text-on-ground pair is chosen to clear 4.5:1 against the worst bone ground it can land on (bone-300), not against the lightest. Audit test: pick the darkest bone a component can sit on and re-check the muted tone.

rules.name: The Kumkum Marks Rule
rules.body: Kumkum red marks the day, the required field, and the error. It never becomes a surface fill larger than a chip, and it never competes with brass for ornament.

rules.name: The Locked Light Rule
rules.body: One theme. There is no .dark block and no toggle by design. Contrast passages are built as ink-800 grounds inside the light world.

rules.name: The Three Register Rule
rules.body: Display, prose, label. Every string on the site belongs to exactly one, and an Indic string belongs to its own serif of the same register. There is no fourth voice and no system-UI display face.

rules.name: The Own Script Rule
rules.body: A city, the brand, and any devotional line carry their own Indic script with a real lang attribute, and both readings stay in the DOM. Script is never a decorative image of language.

rules.name: The No Faux Weight Rule
rules.body: font-synthesis: none on headings, labels and data. A synthesised bold inside a display line is the one type defect that reads as an error.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: Nothing sits above a heading - no eyebrow, no label, no ordinal. Where a small line is needed it goes below the block as a colophon. The only ordinals in the system are the franchise process steps, where the sequence is the information.

rules.name: The One Family Per Section Rule
rules.body: A section states its layout family in its file header and holds it. Repeating a family back-to-back is the failure this rule exists to prevent.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted from the ink, never neutral black, and always carry both offset and blur. A hard offset shadow with no blur does not exist in this world.

rules.name: The Four Materials Rule
rules.body: Leaf, panel, plate, struck. If a new surface needs depth, it takes one of these four or it stays flat on the paper.

rules.name: The Tooth Rule
rules.body: Any large flat bone fill gets the paper tooth. A perfectly flat warm fill reads as a screen colour, and this world is a printed page.

rules.name: The Arrival-Only Rule
rules.body: Motion adds the arrival; it never gates the content. If a reveal fails, the page is still complete and readable.

dos: Do put the paper tooth under any large bone fill, so no flat warm ground reads as a screen colour.
Do rule lists as registers - hairline bone-400 rows with a brass-tinted heading rule and a fixed figure gutter - instead of reaching for card grids.
Do use brass-700 for any brass text below 0.875rem, and keep brass-500/brass-600 on marks, rules, carets and icons.
Do check every muted tone against the darkest bone ground it can land on (bone-300), not the lightest.
Do take depth from exactly one of the four materials - leaf, panel, brass plate, struck - and leave everything else flat.
Do measure prose: 17-26ch for headings and pull statements, 34-46ch for leads, 46-62ch for body.
Do give a section its own layout family, declared in the file header, and never repeat a family in adjacent sections.
Do carry both readings of a bilingual word in the DOM with real lang attributes, so meaning never depends on the animation.
Do mark unconfirmed owner data with the provisional notice material rather than inventing plausible values.
Do route every transition through --ease-almanac and one of the seven named keyframes.
donts: Don't add a dark theme, a .dark block, or a theme toggle. Dark passages are ink-800 grounds inside the one locked light theme.
Don't introduce a second metal or a second accent hue. Brass is the only metal; kumkum only marks.
Don't let kumkum red become a section ground - it stays on diamonds, chips, bullets, errors and the button hover wipe.
Don't round corners past the 0.125rem token. No pills, no circular buttons; the only circle is the lotus roundel.
Don't ship a neutral-black shadow, or a hard offset shadow with no blur. Shadows are ink-tinted with offset and soft blur.
Don't place a kicker, eyebrow, label or ordinal above a heading. Small lines sit below the block as a colophon.
Don't number sections decoratively. The franchise process steps are the only ordinals, because there the sequence is the information.
Don't use gradient text, or glass and blur as decoration. The header's 2px blur exists only to keep type legible over scrolling content on a 97%-opaque band.
Don't use an icon font, an emoji, or a text glyph as an icon. Ornament is authored SVG in the 1.25-stroke language, drawn from the building.
Don't let a synthesised weight ship: keep font-synthesis: none on display, label and data type.
Don't hide content behind a reveal. Authored markup is visible; the arming attribute is added by JS and swept clear on failure.
